guardian.description:
Hakainde Hichilema is bidding for second term, but feud between him and family of Edgar Lungu, who died in 2025, continues

As Zambians go to the polls on Thursday, the ghost of the current president’s predecessor hangs over the elections.

Hakainde Hichilema, 64, is bidding for a second term leading the southern African country after defeating his arch-rival Edgar Lungu by a landslide in 2021.

Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake

At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 as torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture as flooding risks remain high despite rainfall easing

At least four people died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport, and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings.

guardian.description:
Blaze fuelled by hot, dry and windy conditions comes within metres of West Kalimantan rehabilitation centre

Orangutans rescued from wildlife traffickers face a new threat from the record number of fires that have broken out in Indonesia in recent weeks.

Flames have come within metres of an animal rehabilitation centre in West Kalimantan as hot, dry and windy conditions have been amplified by a powerful El Niño and the human-driven climate crisis.

Japanese PM says islands seized by Soviets late in second world war are part of her country under international law

The Japanese government has reacted angrily to Vladimir Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, which are claimed by both Tokyo and Moscow.

Japan’s foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, summoned the Russian ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev, while the prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, called Putin’s actions “absolutely unacceptable”.

rfi.title: A war on words: why Russian strikes are targeting Ukrainian publishers
rfi.description: On 1 August Russian drone strikes on a logistics and distribution centre in northern Kharkiv destroyed more than 8 million books, in a war being waged not just at the frontline, but on Ukraine's culture and identity.

rfi.description: Romania on Thursday began a complete shutdown of its only nuclear plant after levels of water in the River Danube – used to cool the site – fell to a record low, the national nuclear energy company said.

rfi.title: France and 30 other countries condemn Iran's executions of protestors
rfi.description: More than 30 countries, including France, the United Kingdom and Canada, have condemned Iran's use of capital punishment, saying in a joint statement on Wednesday the Islamic Republic was executing protesters to "silence dissent". Tehran accused its critics of hypocrisy.

rfi.title: Russia threatens retaliatory seizures of EU ships amid new sanctions push
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.

rfi.title: Morocco steps up border security over fears of new mass crossing into Ceuta
rfi.description: Morocco has stepped up security along its borders with the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla after fresh calls appeared on social media urging migrants to attempt another mass crossing, weeks after tens of thousands rushed the frontier.

rfi.title: Sister act ushers underdogs Malawi into WAFCON final against Cameroon
rfi.description: Goals from sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga on Wednesday gave tournament outsiders Malawi a 3-1 victory over Algeria, sending them to the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final – after they qualified for the tournament for the first time this year.

rfi.title: Voters in Zambia to deliver verdict on president's economic record
rfi.description: Zambia are voting in a general election on Thursday which will decide whether President Hakainde Hichilema returns for a second term, after steering the country out of a debt crisis.

rfi.title: Can UK's hard-right Farage bin financial probe with by-election win?
rfi.description: Nigel Farage – leader of the anti-immigration Reform UK party – will be fighting for his parliamentary seat on Thursday, going head to head with parody candidate Count Binface in snap polls. The by-election was called after Farage resigned amid a probe into his finances. But the surprise move threatens to backfire as none of the major political parties has fielded a candidate.

rfi.title: Millions gather to watch as solar eclipse plunges swathe of Spain into darkness
rfi.description: Millions of spectators – tourists and locals alike – gathered in parks and cities across Spain to see Wednesday's total solar eclipse, the first of its kind in the country in more than a century.

rfi.title: France gripped by latest summer heatwave as drought conditions worsen
rfi.description: Scorching heat continued to spread across most of mainland France on Wednesday, as the Ministry for Ecological Transition met to take stock of the effects of a drought that has been steadily worsening since May.

rfi.title: Hungary elects Orban critic Andras Baka as first president in new political era
rfi.description: Hungarian lawmakers on Tuesday approved former supreme court chief Andras Baka – a prominent critic of Viktor Orban who was ousted during the ex-premier's time in power – as the country's next head of state.

rfi.title: Assisted dying, social media and agriculture put France’s top court in spotlight
rfi.description: France’s Constitutional Council is facing a politically charged end to the summer, with judges due to rule on a series of high-profile laws – including those covering assisted dying, social media use by children, agriculture and public security.

rfi.title: Lebanon becomes first country in Middle East to abolish death penalty
rfi.description: Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday abolished the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to replace capital punishment with a sentence of life imprisonment with hard labour.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: Race to find Ebola vaccine as DR Congo outbreak kills more than 2,000
rfi.description: The latest outbreak of Ebola has killed more than 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to health authorities. Meanwhile, international efforts have been stepped up to test a vaccine for the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027

euronews.description: Víctor Coyote, the stage name of Víctor María Aparicio Abundancia, died on Thursday in Galicia in a cycling accident. He was 67 and leaves a bold four-decade career spanning music, comics, film and videos.

euronews.title: Survivors tell of horror of Zimbabwe ferry sinking as police say death toll hits 46
euronews.description: The overloaded government ferry, a vital link for villagers and fish traders around the vast Lake Kariba, overturned in choppy waters on Tuesday in one of the country's worst passenger boat disasters.

euronews.title: Explosion rocks ammunition factory near Rome, Italian police say
euronews.description: Italian media reported that there were no casualties, with the AGI news agency saying employees sheltered in secure areas at the facility.

euronews.description: Euronews has gathered the views of experts and local guides on the unusual length of the eruption and on the precautions to take to watch it safely.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi les canicules se répètent-elles en France ? Les questions posées par une succession inédite de vagues de chaleur
lemonde.description: Entre mai et juillet, la France a été le pays le plus anormalement chaud du monde. Le rôle du réchauffement climatique ne fait pas de doute, mais la fréquence des canicules n’avait pas été anticipée. Les causes possibles sont débattues dans la communauté scientifique.

lemonde.title: Le Japon sous le choc après une visite de Vladimir Poutine sur des territoires disputés du sud des îles Kouriles
lemonde.description: Le déplacement du chef de l’Etat russe a été qualifié d’« inacceptable » par la première ministre nippone. Les quatre îles de l’archipel sont administrées par la Russie depuis 1946, mais toujours revendiquées par le Japon qui souhaiterait les récupérer.

lemonde.title: La plateforme des impôts, Impots.gouv.fr, victime d’une cyberattaque

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : une frappe russe a fait un mort et une quinzaine de blessés à Kramatorsk, dans le Donbass
lemonde.description: Le chef de l’administration militaire de l’oblast de Donetsk, Vadym Filachkine, a appelé les habitants locaux à « évacuer vers des régions d’Ukraine plus sûres ». Par ailleurs, une femme de 25 ans et un enfant de 5 ans ont été blessés dans une frappe russe qui a touché l’oblast de Zaporijia.

lemonde.title: « Ces discours politiques ne sont plus audibles dans les casernes et sur le terrain » : les pompiers expliquent les raisons de leur « déception » après leur rencontre avec Laurent Nuñez
lemonde.description: L’intersyndicale des sapeurs-pompiers, qui réclame des moyens supplémentaires pour une profession « à bout », promet une nouvelle mobilisation fin septembre.

lemonde.title: Au Festival de Locarno, la forêt, à la fois lieu de refuge et symbole de la nature en danger, a occupé les écrans
lemonde.description: La 79ᵉ édition du festival de cinéma suisse, qui se clôt samedi 15 août avec la remise du Léopard d’or, a révélé le Vietnamien Lê Bao, réalisateur de l’enivrant « Hearing ».

lemonde.title: Les physalies, animaux marins très urticants, de retour sur les plages du Sud-Ouest
lemonde.description: Depuis le mois de juillet, des échouages massifs de ces organismes se multiplient sur le littoral aquitain. La fréquence et l’ampleur du phénomène interrogent les scientifiques, qui cherchent notamment à déterminer le rôle du changement climatique.

lemonde.title: Les Etats-Unis et le Mexique mènent des exercices à leur frontière commune, là où opère le cartel de Juarez
lemonde.description: L’opération conjointe intervient quelques semaines après que Washington a inscrit le cartel de Juárez sur sa liste des « organisations terroristes étrangères », lui interdisant notamment l’accès au système financier américain.

lemonde.title: Les Emirats arabes unis accusent l’Iran d’avoir attaqué deux navires dans le détroit d’Ormuz
lemonde.description: Abou Dhabi a dénoncé des « actes de piraterie » commis par les gardiens de la révolution iraniens, après cette attaque qui aurait eu lieu jeudi 13 août au soir, selon l’agence de presse officielle ​WAM.

lemonde.title: Après plus de huit mois en mer, les conditions de vie à bord du porte-avions « Abraham-Lincoln » inquiètent
lemonde.description: Des élus démocrates réclament des explications après des signalements de pénuries, de problèmes sanitaires et d’une dégradation de la santé mentale à bord du navire. Le média spécialisé « Navy Times » rapporte que deux marins auraient tenté de se suicider en se jetant par-dessus bord.

lemonde.title: Aujourd’hui, l’Occupation est peu abordée par un théâtre pourtant prompt à s’emparer des sujets politiques
lemonde.description: « Le théâtre sous l’Occupation » (5/5). Ariane Mnouchkine, Julien Gosselin, Stanislas Nordey ou Jeanne Balibar goûtent peu les œuvres créées à Paris durant la guerre. Mais la période incite à se poser une question : que faire si l’extrême droite arrive au pouvoir en 2027 ?

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, trois condamnés à mort exécutés dans la même journée dans trois Etats différents
lemonde.description: Le fait que ces trois injections létales aient eu lieu le même jour est une coïncidence mais cela reflète le rythme soutenu des exécutions aux États-Unis où, depuis le début de l’année, 22 condamnés à mort ont subi la peine capitale.

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, la police remet la main sur des œuvres d’Henri Matisse volées en 2025 à Sao Paulo
lemonde.description: Les œuvres, estimées à environ 200 000 dollars par la police, faisaient partie d’un ensemble de treize illustrations dérobées en décembre dans la bibliothèque Mario de Andrade, au cœur de la plus grande ville du pays.

lemonde.title: Au Japon, des pluies diluviennes font au moins quatre morts à l’est de Tokyo
lemonde.description: Les précipitations ont fortement perturbé les réseaux routier et ferroviaire et bloqué des milliers de personnes à l’aéroport international de Narita, qui dessert la capitale.

lemonde.title: Adieu « fake news », bonjour « FIMI » : le lexique de la désinformation fait peau neuve
lemonde.description: « Dix ans de post-vérité » (4/5). A peine Donald Trump élu en 2016, l’anglicisme « fake news » se diffuse dans le monde entier. Ambigu, malmené et récupéré, il est aujourd’hui remplacé par des termes plus techniques.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump impose 100 % de droits de douane sur certains drones pour contrer les importations chinoises
lemonde.description: Selon la Maison Blanche, le but est d’« encourager la production » de drones aux Etats-Unis, de « réduire la dépendance » à des fournisseurs étrangers et de protéger la sécurité nationale du pays.

france24fr.title: Ferran Torres, héros de la finale de la Coupe du monde, va rejoindre le PSG
france24fr.description: Le Paris Saint-Germain a trouvé un accord avec le FC Barcelone pour l'arrivée de Ferran Torres, auteur du but de la victoire de l'Espagne en finale de la dernière Coupe du monde. L'attaquant de 26 ans devrait rejoindre le champion d'Europe en titre pour un montant estimé à 50M€.

france24fr.title: Législative partielle au Royaume-Uni : Nigel Farage revendique la victoire
france24fr.description: Alors que le dépouillement était toujours en cours vendredi matin à l'aube, Nigel Farage, chef du parti anti-immigration Reform UK, a revendiqué sa victoire à la législative partielle de Clacton, un scrutin qu'il a lui-même provoqué après avoir été rattrapé par des affaires de dons non déclarés. Les partis traditionnels britanniques ont boycotté l'élection.

france24fr.title: Landes, Grèce, Croatie... L'Europe continue de lutter contre les incendies
france24fr.description: Les Landes, dans le sud-ouest de la France, étaient le théâtre dans la nuit de jeudi à vendredi d'un nouvel incendie qui a déjà parcouru 600 hectares et provoqué 500 évacuations. En Croatie, un violent feu de forêt a embrasé des logements dans une localité du littoral, conduisant à l'évacuation de centaines d'habitants et de touristes. Un incendie a par ailleurs éclaté dans le nord de la Grèce, dans la région touristique de Chalcidique, nécessitant l'évacuation de centaines de touristes.

france24fr.title: En direct : Washington menace l'Iran d'un "isolement économique comme le monde n'en a jamais vu"
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire américain au Trésor, Scott Bessent, a menacé, jeudi, de soumettre l'Iran à un isolement économique "comme le monde n'en a jamais vu", avec de nouvelles mesures attendues "la semaine prochaine", en plus du blocus dans le détroit d'Ormuz. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : Donald Trump impose des droits de douane jusqu'à 100 % sur les drones importés
france24fr.description: Afin d'"encourager la production" aux États-Unis et de "réduire la dépendance" à des fournisseurs étrangers, le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé jeudi des droits de douane allant jusqu'à 100% sur les importations de drones et de composants de drones. Dans son viseur : la Chine, qui domine ce marché.

france24fr.title: Mali: le président de la Transition accorde une grâce à un agent français de la DGSE
france24fr.description: Au Mali, le président de la Transition Assimi Goïta a gracié un agent de renseignement français sous statut diplomatique, condamné au Mali à 20 ans de prison en juin, a annoncé jeudi le gouvernement malien dans un communiqué publié sur Facebook. Ce geste de clémence et d'apaisement intervient après des années de fortes tensions entre Paris et Bamako.

france24fr.title: Un "acteur malveillant" a piraté le fisc fin juin, près de 680 000 personnes seraient concernées
france24fr.description: Le système d'information du fisc a été piraté fin juin, a annoncé jeudi le ministère français de l'Économie et des Finances. Selon French Breaches, un site spécialisé dans les cyberattaques, près de 680 000 personnes seraient concernées.

france24fr.title: Colombie : le séisme pèse sur l'industrie du café et toute l'économie
france24fr.description: Le tremblement de Terre qui a secoué la Colombie a été le plus meurtrier depuis le début du siècle et les dégâts matériels sont également considérables : 6,3 milliards de dollars au moins selon les premières estimations, l'équivalent de 1% du PIB du pays. L'industrie du café, pilier de l'économie du pays, est très impactée : la région d'Eje Cafetero est proche de l'épicentre, les infrastructures d'exportation des graines sont endommagées. Le café représente 3 à 4 milliards $ de revenus annuels.

france24fr.title: Côte d'Ivoire : l'urbanisation et l'érosion côtière menacent les cocoteraies
france24fr.description: En Côte d’Ivoire, les cocoteraies reculent face à l’urbanisation et au recul du littoral. Une menace pour des milliers de familles qui en vivent, mais aussi pour la protection des côtes.

france24fr.title: Canicules et sécheresse records: un été catastrophique en France et en Europe
france24fr.description: La vague de chaleur actuelle en France dure depuis 17 jours. Elle a dépassé en longueur celle de 2003. Cet été brûlant a aussi entraîné une sécheresse record en Europe. Au point que les fleuves européens sont à leur plus bas niveau. La Roumanie a dû mettre à l'arrêt son unique centrale nucléaire que le Danube ne pouvait plus refroidir. Le débit du Rhin perturbe le transport fluvial de marchandises. Et une commune de l'est de la France a dû être ravitaillée en eau par camion-citerne.

france24fr.title: À Cuba, Raul Castro réapparaît en public lors d'un hommage à son frère Fidel
france24fr.description: Après plusieurs mois d'absence, l'ex-président cubain Raul Castro, 95 ans, a fait son retour sur la scène publique jeudi à La Havane où il a été ovationné pour le centenaire de la naissance de son frère Fidel. Cet anniversaire survient alors que Cuba traverse l'une des pires crises de son histoire, avec de graves pénuries de nourriture et d'eau, et des coupures d'électricité chroniques.

france24fr.title: Thierry Burkhard, l’ex-chef d’état-major des armées françaises, n’a jamais prononcé ces phrases
france24fr.description: Des internautes attribuent à tort des propos contre l’Ukraine ou critiques envers Emmanuel Macron à l’ancien chef d’état-major des armées françaises, le général Thierry Burkhard. france24fr.title: La visite de Poutine aux îles Kouriles provoque la colère du Japon
france24fr.description: Jeudi 13 août 2026, Vladimir Poutine s’est rendu pour la première fois aux îles Kouriles, un archipel disputé avec le Japon depuis 1945. Une visite qui ravive les tensions entre Moscou et Tokyo, le Japon a déclaré avoir convoqué l’ambassadeur de Russie.

france24fr.title: Avec la sécheresse en France, 40 000 personnes face au risque de pénurie d'eau potable
france24fr.description: Alors qu'une nouvelle canicule s'étend jeudi sur l'Hexagone, des dizaines de communes sont contraintes de se ravitailler en eau potable par camion-citerne ou dons de bouteille tandis que 70 % du territoire fait l'objet de mesures de restrictions des usages en raison de la sécheresse. Certaines localités françaises pourraient-elles venir à manquer d'eau potable ? Éléments de réponse.

Le rachat de Mammut par un fonds chinois révèle le triomphe du secteur de l’alpinisme et des sports de plein air en Chine. Très prisée dans ce pays, la marque suisse devra cultiver son positionnement d’expert pour poursuivre sa croissance

Ce documentaire donne la parole à neuf Palestiniens ayant fui Gaza. Le film l’a emporté sur deux autres productions romandes lors de la sélection organisée pendant le Festival de Locarno

«Qui vit encore» du genevois Nicolas Wadimoff représentera la Suisse dans la course aux Oscars dans la catégorie du meilleur film étranger, a annoncé jeudi l’Office fédéral de la culture. Ce documentaire donn

spiegel.title: Ukrainekrieg: Schwerer russischer Bombenangriff auf Kramatorsk
spiegel.description: Russland hat die frontnahe Stadt Kramatorsk in der Ostukraine erneut mehrfach aus der Luft angegriffen. Die Ukraine meldet mindestens einen Toten und mehrere Verletzte. Anwohnern wird geraten, umzusiedeln.

spiegel.title: SPD-Rentenexpertin schlägt Abschaffung der »Rente mit 63« in fünf Jahren vor
spiegel.description: Teile von SPD und CDU rebellieren gegen die geplante Abschaffung der Frührente. Nun meldet sich die linke SPD-Politikerin Annika Klose zu Wort. Sie hat die Reform mit verhandelt und schlägt nun eine Übergangsfrist vor.

spiegel.title: Lettland: Kampfjets fangen Drohne ab
spiegel.description: Über dem lettischen Luftraum haben Nato-Jets eine Drohne bisher unbekannter Herkunft abgeschossen. Zuvor waren Anwohner aufgerufen, sich in Sicherheit zu bringen. Auch Finnland hat Vorsichtsmaßnahmen ergriffen.

spiegel.title: Hürtgenwald: Waldbrand in der Eifel – NRW-Ortsteil evakuiert
spiegel.description: Die Feuerwehr kämpft gegen einen Waldbrand im nordrhein-westfälischen Kreis Düren. Weil die Flammen einem Teil der Gemeinde Hürtgenwald gefährlich nahekommen, müssen sich nun Hunderte Menschen in Sicherheit bringen.

spiegel.title: Dürre und Hitzewelle: Bauernverband befürchtet in einigen Regionen »totalen Ernteausfall«
spiegel.description: Hitze und Trockenheit haben Folgen für die Landwirtschaft: Vor allem in Süddeutschland dürfte die Ernte schlecht ausfallen, warnt der Bauernverband und fordert von der Regierung Hilfen und billigeren Agrardiesel für Landwirte.

spiegel.title: News: Frust in der SPD, Bandengewalt in Berlin, Futtermangel in der Landwirtschaft
spiegel.description: Die SPD-Chefs ziehen den Zorn der Basis auf sich. Eine Serie von Schutzgelderpressungen erschüttert Berlin. Landwirten geht das Tierfutter aus. Das ist die Lage am Freitagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Obst- und Gemüse-Saisonkalender: Was wächst wann?
spiegel.description: Saisonal kochen steht für: Abwechslung, Flexibilität, Geschmack – und Mut in der Küche. Unser interaktiver Saisonkalender zeigt Ihnen, was gerade reif ist.

spiegel.title: Marmelade kochen, Weckgläser nutzen und Gemüsepaste herstellen: So einfach geht's
spiegel.description: Jantje Schumacher bringt Großstädtern Einkochen, Einmachen und Einlegen bei. Hier erklärt sie, wie einfach es ist, gute Marmelade zu machen – und wie man Weckgläser richtig benutzt.

spiegel.title: Kim Cattrall wird 70
spiegel.description: Die Erfolgsserie »Sex and the City« machte Kim Cattrall zum Star, aber das hatte nicht nur positive Folgen. Jetzt wird Cattrall 70 Jahre alt – und hat Samantha Jones längst hinter sich gelassen.

spiegel.title: A44 bei Diemelstadt in Hessen: Lkw fährt in Rettungswagen auf Standstreifen – mehrere Verletzte
spiegel.description: Dramatische Szenen auf der Autobahn 44 bei Diemelstadt: Dort wurde in Mann in einem Rettungswagen auf dem Seitenstreifen behandelt. Dann fuhr ein Lkw ungebremst in das Fahrzeug.

spiegel.title: US-Zölle von Donald Trump: Importierte Drohnen sollen bis zu 100 Prozent teurer werden
spiegel.description: Mit neuen Zöllen wollen die USA die Abhängigkeit von chinesischen Drohnenherstellern verringern und die heimische Produktion stärken. Durch die Maßnahme könnten auch zwei Söhne des US-Präsidenten profitieren.

spiegel.title: USA vollstrecken drei Todesurteile an einem Tag in Tennessee, Oklahoma und Alabama
spiegel.description: Unter der Trump-Regierung sind US-Bundesstaaten angehalten, verurteilte Mörder hinzurichten. Und viele folgen dieser Direktive eifrig: Zuletzt gleich dreimal binnen 24 Stunden.

spiegel.title: Kuba wirft USA »brutale und unmoralische Belagerung« vor
spiegel.description: In diesen Tagen wäre Revolutionsführer Fidel Castro ein Jahrhundert alt geworden. Auf einer Gala zu seinen Ehren – mit einem Lebenszeichen von Bruder Raúl – fielen in Havanna klare Worte in Richtung der US-Regierung.

spiegel.title: Tirol: Deutscher Wanderer stürzt bei Familienausflug in den Tod
spiegel.description: Ein Mann ist mit Schwiegervater und Schwägern in den Zillertaler Alpen unterwegs. Plötzlich verliert er das Gleichgewicht und stürzt in die Tiefe. Die anderen Männer versuchen, ihn zu retten – vergeblich.

spiegel.title: Kennedy Center: Donald Trumps Name soll an Fassade zurückkehren
spiegel.description: Die Posse um das Kennedy Center in Washington geht in die nächste Runde: Donald Trump besteht weiter darauf, dass sein Name das Kulturzentrum ziert. Ein Gericht lehnte das ab – nun will das Zentrum zu einem Trick greifen.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump ordnet Rückkehr zu Dampfkatapulten auf US-Flugzeugträgern an
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident hat selbst nie in der US-Armee gedient – aber zu Militärthemen trotzdem immer eine klare Meinung. Aktuell im Fokus: Flugzeugträger. Trumps jüngste Anordnung dürfte Milliarden kosten.

spiegel.title: East Sussex: Zug im Südosten Englands entgleist – mehrere Verletzte
spiegel.description: Bilder zeigen umgekippte Waggons, auf einigen stehen Menschen: Im Südosten Englands ist es zu einem Zugunglück gekommen. Mehrere Verletzte wurden in Krankenhäuser gebracht.

spiegel.title: Erling Haaland: Polizei stellt Kokain mit Konterfei des Fußball-Stars sicher
spiegel.description: Sei es auf dem Fußballplatz oder in den sozialen Medien: Erling Haaland ist derzeit omnipräsent. Fahnder in Ecuador haben sein Konterfei nun aber an einem ungewöhnlichen Ort ausgemacht.

elpais.title: Marruecos despliega cientos de policías y militares en la frontera ante los llamamientos a una nueva irrupción masiva
elpais.description: España, que ha aumentado un 42% los policías y guardias civiles en la ciudad, centra sus esfuerzos en expulsar a los 5.000 migrantes irregulares que permanecen e incrementar la presencia de agentes en las calles

elpais.title: Las palabras de Albares activan el temor a la devolución entre los migrantes llegados a nado a Ceuta
elpais.description: La confirmación de la cooperación con Marruecos dispara la preocupación entre quienes llevan dos semanas esperando en condiciones precarias una oportunidad para quedarse en España

elpais.title: Antonio Maíllo: “Marruecos ha cometido una acción criminal con muertes. Hay que replantearse todo”
elpais.description: El coordinador federal de Izquierda Unida defiende en EL PAÍS un cambio total en las relaciones diplomáticas con el país vecino tras la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta

elpais.title: ¿Por qué se ha encarecido más el diésel que la gasolina?
elpais.description: El gasóleo escala más del doble según los últimos datos del IPC. Los expertos apuntan a los exitosos ataques de Ucrania contra las refinerías rusas y a una mayor demanda

elpais.title: La casa del portero es ya un negocio inmobiliario en Madrid: “Reformada, genera unos 1.000 euros al mes para los vecinos”
elpais.description: En la capital cada vez hay más comunidades que financian obras de mejora u otros gastos en sus edificios gracias a lo que sacan por la venta o el alquiler de estos inmuebles, antes reservados para quienes cuidaban de las fincas

elpais.title: La matriarca de las orcas ‘gladis’, de 60 años, aparece con impactos de perdigones en la aleta
elpais.description: El Gobierno abre una investigación y contacta con Portugal, donde las primeras informaciones apuntan a que le dispararon

elpais.title: Anne Hathaway vuelve a reinar en Hollywood: cómo cinco películas, un embarazo y la mejor de sus carcajadas la recolocaron en el trono
elpais.description: Tras una década en la que se convirtió en la más odiada del panorama sin un motivo concreto, la intérprete revienta las taquillas del año gracias a ‘El diablo viste de Prada’ y ‘La odisea’

elpais.title: Nina Lykke: “Los hijos en Noruega están al mando de una forma descabellada. La autoridad está muy denostada”
elpais.description: La autora nórdica, una de las voces más destacadas y cáusticas de la literatura escandinava, se adentra en las difíciles relaciones entre madres e hijos con su última novela: ‘¿Dónde están los adultos?’

elpais.title: ¿Por qué internet se ha obsesionado con un libro de más de 500 páginas sobre la sal?
elpais.description: Publicado originalmente en 2002 y escrito por el periodista estadounidense Mark Kurlansky, ‘Sal. Historia de la única piedra comestible’ está viviendo un inesperado resurgimiento gracias a las redes sociales

elpais.title: Así son las vacaciones más saludables, según la ciencia: mejor largas y con actividad deportiva de por medio
elpais.description: Un metaanálisis constata que el descanso laboral favorece el bienestar, pero los expertos avisan de que en los parones veraniegos también puede hacer aflorar el agotamiento acumulado

elpais.title: “Mirad sus brazos. Está buenísimo”: el auge de los políticos guapos se hace viral
elpais.description: La presencia en redes del candidato a senador estadounidense Abdul El-Sayed desata un debate más amplio sobre la relación entre fotogenia y éxito político

elpais.title: Ceuta, de los tacticismos banales a la mirada estratégica
elpais.description: España debe tener en cuenta en su política migratoria la extrema sensibilidad actual de los socios y aliados

elpais.title: El ‘momento Aranzadi’ de Vox
elpais.description: La ultraderecha ya no quiere ser antisistema en las formas, sino utilizar los resortes del Estado para transformarlo

elpais.title: Hacienda limita la rebaja fiscal al vender el piso de soltero para comprar una casa en pareja
elpais.description: El Tribunal Económico-Administrativo fija criterio y establece que el incentivo fiscal depende de la cuota de propiedad y no del dinero aportado por cada cónyuge

elpais.title: Trump extiende sus tentáculos militares en Latinoamérica
elpais.description: Hegseth anuncia que no descarta una opción militar en La Habana y plantea operaciones en suelo colombiano. La estrategia de Trump para controlar la región choca con la resistencia de México y la sumisión de Centroamérica

elpais.title: Flávio Bolsonaro sufre problemas para inscribir su candidatura presidencial al aparecer en un partido distinto al suyo
elpais.description: El incidente, a dos días del fin del plazo, enrarece el ambiente en Brasil, marcado por la polarización y las sospechas

elpais.title: Las siete vidas de Daniela
elpais.description: El terremoto fue la última batalla con la muerte de Daniela Largo, una superviviente rescatada en Pereira tras 36 horas bajo los escombros

elpais.title: La “carrera de obstáculos” de las afganas para pedir el traslado a España: años de espera, documentos “imposibles” y recursos judiciales
elpais.description: Las embajadas españolas en Irán y Pakistán deniegan un número creciente de peticiones de víctimas de los talibanes, según varias ONG

nyt.title: Trump Gives Green Light to U.S. Companies to Aim Hacks at Cybercriminals
nyt.description: The practice would align the United States more closely with countries like China and Russia, where spy agencies have long relied on private-sector hackers to help with national security missions.

nyt.title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Has Been Deployed for Months, Prompting Concerns
nyt.description: The U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln has been deployed for nearly nine months. Members of Congress are worried about the crew’s well-being.

nyt.title: American Missionary Kidnapped in Niger Is Said to Be Released From Captivity
nyt.description: The release of Kevin Rideout, an American missionary pilot who was seized in Niger’s capital last fall, has been a priority for the White House.

nyt.title: Judge Dismisses Trump Administration’s Antisemitism Case Against Harvard
nyt.description: The government argued the university had not done enough to combat antisemitism during campus protests. A judge called the incidents “isolated and episodic.”

nyt.title: Deaths of 3 ICE Detainees Prompt Questions About Medical Care
nyt.description: Immigrants at Delaney Hall in Newark have complained about health services. Federal officials defended the treatment provided there and elsewhere.

nyt.title: Appeals Court Sidesteps Key Question Over Trump’s Use of Alien Enemies Act
nyt.description: The court dismissed a case over the Alien Enemies Act in a messy conclusion to a long-running legal battle that had seemed destined to end up before the Supreme Court.

nyt.title: Trump’s Immigration Policy Echoes 1920s Crackdown, but This Time Congress Isn’t Involved
nyt.description: U.S. leaders limited immigration amid economic and social turmoil. Historians see similarities to Trump’s crackdown, with a catch: He’s doing it without Congress.

nyt.title: Afghan Women Erased From Public Life in Five Years of Taliban Rule
nyt.description: Decrees restricting the rights of women and girls to study, work, travel and act independently now threaten to damage Afghanistan permanently, experts say.

nyt.title: What to Know About Luigi Mangione’s Court Cases and Potential Plea Deal
nyt.description: Mr. Mangione faces federal charges of stalking that resulted in the death of a health insurance executive. A guilty plea could close the federal case — and complicate a separate state murder trial.

nyt.title: The Golden Age of Mexican Food Is Here. And It’s Complicated.
nyt.description: Even at a time of anti-immigration politics, there has never been a richer variety of Mexican restaurants in the United States.

nyt.title: 41 of the Greatest Mexican Restaurants In the United States
nyt.description: Our favorite choices for seafood from Sonora, carnitas from Michoacán, chalupas from Puebla and so much more.

nyt.title: California May Let Residents Choose ‘Jewish’ as an Ethnic Identifier
nyt.description: A bill would allow Jews to identify themselves as an ethnic group on state forms. Supporters argue it’s a step toward acknowledging the complex nature of Jewish identity.

nyt.title: A City Mobilizes Against a Stubborn Health Threat: Mosquitoes
nyt.description: The city of Belém in northern Brazil was overwhelmed by an outbreak of dengue two years ago. An all-out municipal effort has reduced cases and may offer lessons to American cities.

nyt.title: How a Long-Shot U.S. Oil Drilling Project Is Shaking Up Greenland
nyt.description: A U.S. oil company says it could be on the verge of a major discovery in Greenland. The proposal comes at a tricky time for the Arctic island, and locals are lining up against it.

nyt.title: Israeli Settlers Resume West Bank Siege After Eviction
nyt.description: The military’s failure to keep extremists away from two Palestinian families trapped in their West Bank homes made clear the chaos gripping the Israeli-occupied territory.

nyt.title: Charlie Kirk Suspect Fights Death Penalty, Says No Others Were in Danger
nyt.description: Prosecutors say they can seek the death penalty against Tyler Robinson because he also endangered people near Charlie Kirk, who was shot in the throat last year. Mr. Robinson’s lawyers note that the gunman struck only his target.

nyt.title: Outdated American Policy Is Hurting the Afghan People
nyt.description: A new generation of Afghans wants to move on from the animosities of the past, but Western policies make that difficult.

nyt.title: Hamas Has No More Cards to Play
nyt.description: The signs point to Hamas being serious about disarming. The recent Board of Peace plan for it to surrender its weapons should be carried out.

republika.title: Lavorare all'estero conviene? Stipendi, diritti e agevolazioni: come funziona negli altri Paesi Ue
republika.description: Compenso più alto non significa sempre più soldi in tasca. Tra costo della vita, tasse, mensilità aggiuntive, Tfr e welfare, il vantaggio di lavorare all'estero cambia molto da Paese a Paese. republika.description: Non solo Roma e Madrid, ben otto Paesi hanno reintrodotto i controlli alle frontiere. Una misura eccezionale contro immigrazione irregolare e terrorismo sta diventando la regola e spesso viene usata per ragioni politiche. L’esperto: “Così la libera circolazione è a rischio”

republika.description: L’attacco del sottosegretario Fazzolari (FdI): “Quella trasmissione ha perso credibilità”. M5S: “Altro che garantisti”

republika.description: L’atto dell’organismo interno all’ad Rossi. Contestata l’amicizia del giornalista con l’arrestato. A Viale Mazzini i timori per la possibile fuga degli investitori pubblicitari dal programma

republika.title: Zaccaria: “Ranucci resta la parte offesa. L’azienda lo difenda”
republika.description: L’ex presidente Rai: “Un giornalista non è un magistrato che ha l’obbligo di stare attento a chi frequenta. Può vedere persone di varia natura per ricavarne delle notizie”

republika.description: A metà del febbraio scorso fui contattato dall’ex direttore de L’Avanti. Mi disse: “Sta per scendere in campo un big”

republika.description: Cisgiordania, l’esercito dello Stato ebraico non argina gli estremisti che da sei giorni circondano tre abitazioni. I residenti non cedono. Il silenzio del premier Netanyahu

republika.title: “In Cisgiordania dall’Italia per aiutare le famiglie, adesso temiamo un’incursione militare”
republika.description: La voce da una delle case assediate: “I soldati hanno tagliato i cavi della videosorveglianza, era una delle poche forme di protezione, ci consentiva di vedere fuori”

republika.title: Case assediate in Cisgiordania: “Le bambine terrorizzate chiedevano perché quei ragazzi ci odiano”
republika.description: Al telefono dalle case strette dalla morsa degli estremisti ebraici, parlano Aisha e Qusay: “Le piccole evacuate, vomitavano”

republika.title: Kabul, cinque anni di talebani: “Donne cancellate, esecuzioni e povertà”
republika.description: Nell’agosto del 2021 gli americani lasciarono l’Afghanistan: “Fame e zero libertà di stampa, il Paese è ripiombato nella paura”

republika.title: Afghanistan, il racconto della dottoressa: “Io, ginecologa in ospedale tra pazienti terrorizzate”
republika.description: La condizione delle donne cinque anni dopo il ritorno dei talebani: “Oggi non ci è permesso studiare, ma lasciano lavorare le dottoresse già specializzate. Il mondo vede sui social cosa ci succede, ma a chi importa davvero?”

republika.title: Congelamento degli ovuli, anche Forza Italia apre. “Serve un’intesa bipartisan”
republika.description: A settembre saranno quattro le proposte di legge depositate in Parlamento per rendere il percorso accessibile alle donne con il contributo pubblico

republika.description: L’europarlamentare del Carroccio: “A 38 anni avevo paura di non aver più tempo per diventare madre. La fertilità femminile non ha colori politici, parliamone a scuola nelle lezioni di educazione civica. Sbagliato escludere le single”

republika.title: Social freezing, Alessia Cappello: “Era un tabù, tornassi indietro non esiterei”
republika.description: Assessora di Italia Viva a Milano, 41 anni: “Mia figlia è arrivata dopo un percorso difficilissimo, ma quindici anni fa nessuno parlava di congelare gli ovuli”

republika.title: La senatrice Cattaneo: “Il Ponte sullo Stretto è stato bocciato, confermati i nostri dubbi”
republika.description: Per ricercatrice il parere tecnico ricalca quello che la scienza ripete da tempo: “Servono ancora altri approfondimenti”

republika.title: Piantedosi avvisa la Germania: “Dalle ong duemila migranti”. Meloni: avanti sulle espulsioni
republika.description: Il ministro: “Compensazioni con Berlino”. E alla Spagna: “Stop ai controlli? Solo se Ceuta è sicura”. Schlein: “La premier imita Trump”

republika.description: La comunicazione formale del Viminale all’esecutivo tedesco che ha annunciato la volontà di rimpatriare in Italia alcuni stranieri

npr.title: Hit hard by the earthquake in western Colombia, the mayor of Cali gets to work
npr.description: Search efforts continue though hopes are fading as teams dig for survivors from the 7.4 magnitude earthquake that killed more than 250 people.

npr.description: U.S. ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee called settlers besieging a West Bank home of an American-Palestinian family "terrorists."

npr.title: Vladimir Putin's first visit to disputed Pacific islands draws Tokyo protest
npr.description: The four southernmost islands of the chain also are claimed by Japan, which calls them the Northern Territories.

npr.title: By sky and sea, Ukraine's drone strikes challenge Russia's grip on Crimea
npr.description: Russia maintained an iron grip on Crimea since seizing it from Ukraine in 2014. Many Russian civilians go there to enjoy the beaches. But now Ukraine is hitting Crimea hard, upending daily life.

npr.title: Taiwan briefly slows its mobile internet to text-only speed as part of defense drill
npr.description: The drills come amid rising tensions with China, which frequently sends military planes and ships towards Taiwan.

npr.description: Inflation cooled a bit last month, according to a new report from the Labor Department. And, ICE plans to equip its officers with electric shock gloves.

npr.description: The U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned the actions of Jewish settlers who are besieging the home of an American Palestinian family in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

npr.title: Millions crowd cities to see Spain's first total solar eclipse in over a century

phys-org.title: Why has Britain's grass turned yellow? A plant scientist explains what happens next
phys-org.description: Fields, parks and lawns across Europe have turned to straw this summer. Landscapes thousands of years old have been revealed as green outlines against yellow backgrounds, where ancient underground walls and ditches retain enough water to sustain pockets of grass above them. Lawns and parklands have been especially affected because what water is available is being directed to homes and farms.

phys-org.title: Teens are turning to AI chatbots for emotional support—here's how to keep kids safe
phys-org.description: It's 2 a.m., and a teenage girl, worrying about an issue with a friend, lies awake. Rather than wake her parents, she picks up her phone, opens an AI app and types, "I'm so stressed out, I can't sleep."

phys-org.title: Two oceans, one country—and 20 times more sharks in the prehistoric Pacific
phys-org.description: How many sharks should a coral reef have? It sounds like a simple question, but almost nowhere on Earth is there a reef that has not at some time been fished or otherwise affected by humans, so there is no yardstick against which to measure what has been lost or what recovery would look like.

phys-org.title: Layered nano-biohybrid uses sunlight, air and water to make hydrogen peroxide
phys-org.description: A research team led by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory has developed a new material that combines inorganic material with biological components to produce hydrogen peroxide more efficiently.

phys-org.title: Fulfilling friendships linked to better health and well-being across 22 countries
phys-org.description: Fulfilling friendships and close social relationships are strongly linked to excellent physical and mental health, finds a substantial global study published in the Journal of Mental Health.

phys-org.title: Tracer exchange reveals ions can speed up or slow down inside battery solids
phys-org.description: Understanding how ions diffuse in solid materials is essential for technologies including batteries, electronics and chemical catalysts, but it has been hard for a simple reason: the materials are solids.

phys-org.title: Theoretical framework expands directional light control beyond ordered crystal structures
phys-org.description: A research team has developed a new theoretical framework that can suppress light scattering in certain directions while enhancing it in others, even in irregularly arranged materials. The work extends research on controlling light scattering, which has traditionally centered on ordered crystal structures, into the realm of disordered systems.

phys-org.title: Synchronized star pairs unleash radio bursts via a Jupiter-Io-like mechanism
phys-org.description: Researchers have helped unravel the mystery of why certain pairs of stars pulse with regular, long-period bursts of radio waves. The particular class of objects observed comes in pairs that always include a compact dead star, called a white dwarf, locked in orbit with an M dwarf, a red star smaller than our sun.

phys-org.title: Butterfly effects of climate change
phys-org.description: The Australian National Insect Collection at CSIRO holds 2,000 drawers of butterfly specimens, including some that were collected more than a century ago.

phys-org.title: Mutation hotspots help 'friendly' viruses outmaneuver the bacteria in your gut
phys-org.description: Every 15 minutes, someone in the U.S. dies from a drug-resistant superbug. A few decades from now, antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections threaten to become the leading cause of death worldwide, outpacing cancer.

phys-org.title: While Great Lakes ice cover is slipping, a 'temporary respite' may be on the way
phys-org.description: There's good news and bad news for folks who love a good coat of ice on the Great Lakes for the activities and businesses it supports. The good news is that, after decades of declining annual average ice cover, there's reason to believe that trend could slow or even temporarily reverse. That's according to new research from the Cooperative Institute for Great Lakes Research, or CIGLR, at the University of Michigan.

phys-org.title: Proposed 900-telescope array could detect an Earth-like exoplanet's atmosphere in a single transit
phys-org.description: What do you do when the observation you need comes around once a year? Well, preparation is key, but this is the awkward truth about finding another Earth. When a planet crosses the face of its star, a sliver of starlight passes through its atmosphere on the way to us, and the gases there absorb their own particular colors. Read the spectrum carefully and you can list what the air is made of: oxygen, ozone and water vapor, the things that would make you sit up.

phys-org.title: How a mystery kept in London led to the discovery of a new Ecuadorian frog
phys-org.description: Scientists from the Pontificia Universidad Católica del Ecuador officially described Pristimantis milpe, an abundant and widely distributed species that had been confused with another species for more than a century. To solve the mystery, researchers reviewed historical specimens collected in Ecuador during the 19th century and preserved at the Natural History Museum in London.

phys-org.title: Safe havens protect Australian mammals from invasive predators. Why aren't they working for other animal groups?
phys-org.description: Feral cats and foxes now roam across almost all of Australia. These predators are a major reason why many species have been driven to extinction.

phys-org.title: How to fine-tune molecular structures within vaccines to improve immune responses
phys-org.description: A vaccine's molecular structure plays a key role in determining how the immune system responds and prepares to protect the body from future exposure to a specific pathogen. To develop a vaccine that offers long-term protection from HIV, it's essential to promote a long-lasting immune response in which immune cells and antibodies prepared to combat the virus persist within the body. This has inspired scientists to find ways to alter vaccine structure to increase the duration and persist

phys-org.title: TESS discovers a rare brown dwarf orbiting a massive, aging star
phys-org.description: For decades, astronomers lumped brown dwarfs into a single category defined by mass alone—too big to be classified as planets but too small to become stars. However, this definition ignores the two very different mechanisms that can form them: the direct collapse of gas clouds and formation within the accretion disks of massive stars.

phys-org.title: How environmental responsibility can improve financial performance
phys-org.description: Consumers are increasingly choosing products from companies that demonstrate genuine environmental responsibility. While many studies have linked environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance with stronger financial results, exactly how environmental responsibility translates into higher profits has remained unclear. A new study suggests that sustainability improves corporate financial performance indirectly by increasing sales.

phys-org.title: There's nothing 'wild' about most wildfires. Humans start them and have made them more dangerous
phys-org.description: A wildfire needs a name long before anyone knows what caused it. When the pines of the Gironde in southwestern France caught fire in July, the fire was reported within hours under the name of the ground it was burning. By the time it had taken 40,000 hectares (99,000 acres), that name was fixed in every bulletin in Europe.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

crunchbase.title: AI-Native, Not AI-Sprinkle: Why AI Is A Business Change, Not A Technology Change
